facts.raw_span: purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet
dusky purpuric macules and patches on her nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear
reticulated purpuric macules and patches on her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms
skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL)
Acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL)
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels (cryocrit, 16%)
Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi supports this diagnosis.
The patient's hypercalcemia, abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses, and monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis are consistent with multiple myeloma.
The patient's presentation with cryoglobulinemia and monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis could also be consistent with Waldenström's macroglobulinemia.

rationales.F01: Purpuric lesions are a common manifestation of cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F02: Dusky purpuric macules and patches are consistent with cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F03: Reticulated purpuric macules and patches are seen in cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F07: Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear are highly suggestive of cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F08: Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses is a key feature of multiple myeloma and cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F09: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis is a strong indicator of cryoglobulinemia and multiple myeloma.
rationales.F10: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels are diagnostic of cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F12: Multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi is characteristic of cryoglobulinemia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, and bone marrow biopsy showing 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction strongly support Multiple Myeloma, while Cryoglobulinemia is also a consideration due to the presence of cryoglobulins and purpuric lesions.
